newsitem.title: USA: Midwest Grain to buy back 200,000 shares.
newsitem.headline: Midwest Grain to buy back 200,000 shares.

text.p: Midwest Grain Products Inc said Thursday its directors authorized the repurchase of up to 200,000 shares of the company's common stock on the open market or through private transactions.
The company said the decision was prompted by the company's strong cash position and the current price of Midwest Grain stock, which closed at $11.375 yesterday.

Rather than reinstating a cash dividend at this time, directors concluded stockholder value would be better served with a modest repurchase program in light of the current market price, the company said in a statement.

"Although our recently announced net income of $862,000 for the first nine months of fiscal 1997 reflects relatively modest results, our earnings before interest, taxes and depreciation for that period were $14 million, or $1.43 per share," said Ladd Seaberg, president and chief executive officer.

"This level of cash flow, together with our strong balance sheet should allow us to finance modest stock repurchases while continuing with reductions in our long-term debt, which have amounted to $8 million in the current fiscal year," he said.
Midwest Grain produces wheat gluten, premium wheat starch and alcohol products made from grain, namely wheat, corn and milo.
